title: `update_transactions` (MCP) clears `original_order` on updated rows
body:
Every row touched by the MCP `update_transactions` tool after the
last sync_down ended up with `original_order = NULL` (7/7 affected rows in our database).
NULL sorts last, so on the next `sync up` those rows are written at the **very bottom of
the Transactions tab — below the oldest row — regardless of date**.

**Root cause (confirmed in source):** `get_transaction_impl` in `src/db/mod.rs` omits
`original_order` from its SELECT and fills the struct with `..Default::default()`
(→ `None`); `update_transaction_impl` then writes **all** columns back, binding that
`None` as NULL. Fetch-incomplete / write-complete asymmetry. The categories and autocat
getters both include the column, so only transactions is affected.

**Fix** (applied to our local build 2026-08-07; patch at the bottom of this issue):
add `original_order` to the SELECT and populate the field. Includes a regression test
(`test_update_transactions_preserves_original_order`) verified to FAIL on the unpatched
code and pass with the fix; all 180 tests pass. Also verified end-to-end over MCP stdio
against a database copy.

---

### Patch

```diff
diff --git a/src/commands/update.rs b/src/commands/update.rs
index 246bd2c..354ca29 100644
--- a/src/commands/update.rs
+++ b/src/commands/update.rs
@@ -196,6 +196,50 @@ mod tests {
         assert_eq!(updated.account_number, "1234");
     }
 
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn test_update_transactions_preserves_original_order() {
+        let env = TestEnv::new().await;
+        let txn_id = "test-txn-order";
+        env.insert_test_transaction(txn_id).await;
+
+        // insert_test_transaction goes through Transactions::parse, which assigns
+        // original_order from the row index — so the row starts with Some(_).
+        let before = env
+            .config()
+            .db()
+            ._get_transaction(txn_id)
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .unwrap();
+        assert!(
+            before.original_order.is_some(),
+            "precondition: inserted row should carry an original_order"
+        );
+
+        let updates = TransactionUpdates {
+            note: Some("touched".to_string()),
+            ..Default::default()
+        };
+        let args = UpdateTransactionsArgs::new(vec![txn_id], updates).unwrap();
+        update_transactions(env.config(), args).await.unwrap();
+
+        // The update must not clobber original_order: the fetch-for-update used to
+        // omit the column, so the write-back stored NULL and the row sank below the
+        // oldest row of the sheet on the next sync up.
+        let after = env
+            .config()
+            .db()
+            ._get_transaction(txn_id)
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(
+            after.original_order, before.original_order,
+            "update_transactions must preserve original_order"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(after.note, "touched");
+    }
+
     #[tokio::test]
     async fn test_update_transactions_not_found_error() {
         let env = TestEnv::new().await;
diff --git a/src/db/mod.rs b/src/db/mod.rs
index 8f27d34..7a0f89c 100644
--- a/src/db/mod.rs
+++ b/src/db/mod.rs
@@ -606,7 +606,7 @@ impl Db {
                 transaction_id, date, description, amount, account, account_number,
                 institution, month, week, full_description, account_id, check_number,
                 date_added, merchant_name, category_hint, category, note, tags,
-                categorized_date, statement, metadata, other_fields
+                categorized_date, statement, metadata, other_fields, original_order
             FROM transactions WHERE transaction_id = ?"#,
         )
         .bind(id)
@@ -663,6 +663,7 @@ impl Db {
                     statement: r.get::<Option<String>, _>("statement").unwrap_or_default(),
                     metadata: r.get::<Option<String>, _>("metadata").unwrap_or_default(),
                     other_fields,
+                    original_order: r.get::<Option<u64>, _>("original_order"),
                     ..Default::default()
                 }))
             }
```

Happy to open a PR.

---
_tiller-sync v0.2.1 (crates.io), macOS, against a ~14k-transaction production Tiller sheet._
